pricing.faqTrialEndsQ: What happens when my trial ends?
pricing.faqTrialEndsA: Pro features lock, but your garden profile, plots, members, and all your data remain intact. You can subscribe anytime to unlock everything again.
pricing.faqDuesQ: How do online dues payments work?
pricing.faqDuesA: Connect your garden’s Stripe account from the billing page (the setup happens right in the app) and members can pay dues online. Payments go directly to your garden, and collection status is tracked automatically.
pricing.faqMultiQ: We run multiple gardens — how does pricing work?
pricing.faqMultiA: Networks and city programs get volume pricing per garden with centralized billing and network-wide impact reporting. Contact us below and we’ll put together a plan for your organization.
pricing.faqMktNeedProQ: Do I need Garden Pro to use the marketplace?
pricing.faqMktNeedProA: No. The marketplace is completely free for growers and buyers. Garden Pro is only for community garden organizers who need advanced management tools.
pricing.faqSmartPricingA: Our algorithm considers local supply levels, sales velocity, and listing freshness to suggest fair market prices. Your price stays within a floor and ceiling you control — it never changes without your input.
pricing.networkBody: Running 5, 50, or 200 gardens? Get volume pricing per garden, centralized billing and administration, online dues collection across every site, and network-wide impact reporting for boards, funders, and councils.

about.yardharvestStartedWithASimple: YardHarvest started with a simple observation on a summer evening in 2024. In neighborhoods across Omaha — from Dundee to Elkhorn, Benson to Bellevue — backyard gardens were overflowing. Tomatoes ripened faster than families could eat them. Zucchini multiplied like magic. Herb gardens grew lush and fragrant while most of the harvest went unused.
about.atTheSameTimeJust: At the same time, just a few blocks away, neighbors were buying plastic-wrapped produce trucked in from hundreds of miles away — produce that was days or even weeks old before it hit the shelf.
about.thatIsHowYardharvestWas: That is how YardHarvest was born — a marketplace built specifically for Omaha's backyard gardeners and the neighbors who love truly fresh, local food. No commercial farms. No industrial agriculture. Just people growing food and sharing it with the folks next door.
about.thatObservationGrewIntoYardharvest: That observation grew into YardHarvest. As we worked with growers, we kept meeting the people who make local food possible at scale: community garden organizers — volunteers, nonprofit program managers, and city parks staff — running plots, dues, waitlists, and workdays out of spreadsheets, paper folders, and group texts.
about.soThatIsWhatYardharvest: So that is what YardHarvest became: a management platform built specifically for community gardens and the organizations behind them. Less time on admin and chasing payments, more time growing food, building community, and proving impact to the funders and councils who keep gardens alive.
about.seoDescription: YardHarvest's story and mission: making community gardens easier to run and helping local garden networks thrive.
about.weThoughtFull: We thought: what if we could connect these two groups? What if the gardener with fifty pounds of tomatoes could easily find the neighbor who would love to buy a few pounds of vine-ripened heirlooms? What if we could turn surplus into income and reduce food waste at the same time?

about.gardenFaq1A: It is free for gardeners and members. Garden organizers get a 14-day free trial of Garden Pro, then choose a monthly or annual plan. Networks and city programs running multiple gardens get volume pricing — see the Pricing page.
about.gardenFaq2Q: What is included for free vs. Garden Pro?
about.gardenFaq2A: Free covers your garden profile and member directory, plot assignments, waitlist and reservations, events with RSVPs, announcements, harvest logging, resource inventory, and the community wall with AI moderation. Garden Pro adds dues and expense management, volunteer shift scheduling, the photo wall with likes & comments, tool checkout and maintenance tracking, broadcast and direct messaging, custom email branding, the plot grid designer, and CSV data export.
about.gardenFaq3Q: How do online dues payments work?
about.gardenFaq3A: Connect your garden’s Stripe account in a few minutes (it never leaves the app) and members can pay dues online by card. Payments go directly to your garden, and the platform tracks who has paid, who is partial, and who needs a reminder.
about.gardenFaq4Q: We run multiple gardens — can we manage them together?
about.gardenFaq4A: Yes. Nonprofits and city programs can run any number of gardens under one organization with volume pricing, centralized administration, and network-wide impact reporting. Contact us from the Pricing page.
about.gardenFaq5Q: Can we produce reports for funders and councils?
about.gardenFaq5A: Yes — harvest pounds, food-bank donations, volunteer hours, participation, and dues collection are tracked automatically and exportable, so seasonal impact reports take minutes instead of days.
about.gardenFaq6Q: What happens to our data if we cancel?
about.gardenFaq6A: Nothing is deleted. Pro features lock, but your garden profile, members, plots, and history remain intact, and you can export your data at any time.
about.mktFaq1Q: How do I sign up as a seller?
about.mktFaq1A: Just create a free YardHarvest account and navigate to "Sell" to create your first listing. Add a photo, set your price and quantity, and you are live! There are no upfront fees.
about.mktFaq2Q: Is there a fee for using YardHarvest?
about.mktFaq2A: YardHarvest is free to browse and buy. We keep the platform running through a small service fee on completed transactions. Sellers keep the vast majority of every sale.
about.mktFaq3Q: How does pickup and delivery work?
about.mktFaq3A: When a buyer places an order, the seller can offer porch pickup, a meeting point, or local delivery. Details are arranged through our built-in messaging system after the order is placed.
about.mktFaq4Q: What if something is wrong with my order?
about.mktFaq4A: We encourage buyers and sellers to communicate directly through our messaging feature. If you receive produce that does not match the listing, you can leave an honest review and reach out to support.
about.mktFaq5A: Our system adjusts effective prices based on local supply and demand. When a vegetable is in high demand and low supply, prices may increase slightly. When supply is abundant, prices stay low. This keeps the marketplace fair and responsive.
about.mktFaq6Q: Do I need a license to sell my garden produce?
about.mktFaq6A: Nebraska has a Cottage Food Law that allows you to sell certain homegrown produce without a special license. YardHarvest is designed for backyard gardeners sharing surplus. Always check local regulations for your specific situation.
about.mktFaq7Q: How far away can buyers be?
about.mktFaq7A: You can set a delivery/pickup radius on your listings. Most transactions happen within a 10-mile radius, but our search lets buyers look up to 50 miles away for specialty items.
about.mktFaq8Q: Can I sell preserved goods like jams or pickles?
about.mktFaq8A: Potentially! Nebraska cottage food laws cover certain preserved items. Check your local guidelines. If allowed, you can list them on YardHarvest with the appropriate category.
